7H Paragraph 7.14 (ii) applies if inextricably linked material is seized under the Criminal Justice
and Police Act 2001, sections 50 or 51. Inextricably linked material is material it is not
reasonably practicable to separate from other linked material without prejudicing the use of

that other material in any investigation or proceedings. For example, it may not be possible
to separate items of data held on computer disk without damaging their evidential integrity.
Inextricably linked material must not be examined, imaged, copied or used for any purpose
other than for proving the source and/or integrity of the linked material.
7HA Further details, including the conditions that must be satisfied before a judge may grant an
application for a warrant authorising retention under the urgent case premises search
power, can be found in paragraph 15A of Schedule 5 to the Terrorism Act 2000 and
paragraph 13 of Schedule 2 to the National Security Act 2023.
